principle: Admit themes, not template volume. Any future quest must be authored around a distinct operational problem and may not recreate item-by-item storefront, body-count, map-copy, mastery, or handover conveyors.

evidence: legacy README defines 283 quests
purpose is unlocking barter/purchase trades for ammunition types and better magazines
chains are coupled to Weapon Proficiency unlocks by caliber
reviews.reason: The frozen Admiral campaign already owns a compact quest-gated munitions capability layer. Porting the legacy ammunition conveyor would duplicate that authority and massively expand storefront progression.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: No ammo-by-ammo quest conveyor, no magazine unlock ladder, and no duplicate permanent ammunition capability outside the existing authored Munitions milestones.

evidence: legacy README defines 92 quests
weapon categories are split into Rookie, Seasoned, Veteran and Elite tiers
barter quests unlock subsequent proficiency quests and storefront progression
reviews.reason: The source is a tiered weapon/storefront progression system. Admiral already has authored Arsenal capability milestones, so direct reuse would create a second overlapping weapon progression engine.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: No four-tier mastery ladder, no weapon-by-weapon unlock conveyor, and no duplicate Arsenal authority; future use is limited to source inventory or a materially distinct one-off operation.

evidence: legacy README defines 1702 quests
bundle is a series of elimination quests with specific weapons
chains are distributed across Fence and location traders
reviews.reason: This is template-volume mastery content rather than a finite Admiral campaign. Its scale and per-weapon repetition are directly contrary to the curated authored-product model.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: Never materialize mastery by weapon enumeration or repeated kill quotas. Any future weapon operation must solve one distinct tactical problem and remain small.

evidence: legacy README defines 920 quests
four chains revolve around handing over requested items
container rewards are issued at completion quartiles
reviews.reason: Nine hundred twenty handover errands are collection busywork and reward-volume inflation. Procurement can fit Admiral only when it supports a specific operation with a clear why/what/payoff.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: No generic requested-item queue, no percent-completion container ladder, and no high-volume handover sequence; any future procurement quest must be singular and contextual.

evidence: legacy README defines 27 quests
quests revolve around finding keys and unlocking rewards
chain moves from Fence to local map traders
reviews.reason: Access intelligence is thematically compatible with Admiral, but a key-collection progression risks becoming another acquisition checklist and may overlap vanilla location progression.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: Future use must be a compact access/reconnaissance operation with vanilla/Scorpion/Artem overlap proof; no key-by-key collection ladder and no broad permanent key storefront.

evidence: legacy README defines location chains with kill counts from 1 through 500 PMCs
the same progression template repeats across locations
later rounds depend on earlier repeated rounds
reviews.reason: A hostile-operator contract can fit Admiral, but 70 quests built from escalating per-map counts are pure template repetition.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: At most a few authored operations with explicit location/context; no 1-to-500 ladder and no copy of the same objective across every map.

evidence: legacy README defines location chains with counts from 1 through 1000 Scavs
the same ten-step counter pattern repeats per location
progression is body-count volume rather than changing tactical requirements
reviews.reason: The source is a large farming ladder and duplicates common vanilla/repeatable combat space. It has little unique Admiral product value in direct form.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: No cumulative Scav farming ladder, no four-digit kill requirement and no map-template duplication; future use requires a genuinely distinct operational threat context.

evidence: legacy README defines a ten-step Raider chain
counts escalate from 1 through 100
the chain is tied to The Labs
reviews.reason: Labs security disruption is compatible with Admiral's access/capability identity, but ten escalating Raider counters add grind rather than new operational meaning.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: Use only a compact Labs-specific operation if it is distinct from frozen Access progression; no 1-to-100 Raider ladder and no reward that bypasses existing Labs clearance authority.

evidence: legacy README defines a ten-step Rogue chain
counts escalate from 1 through 100
source deliberately permits completion outside Lighthouse when spawn mods are present
reviews.reason: A Rogue operation can be distinctive, but the legacy version is still only a count ladder and its location-free compatibility rule weakens authored context.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: Future use must have explicit operational context and bounded target count; no 1-to-100 ladder and no location-free farming rule solely for mod compatibility.

evidence: legacy README defines per-location PMC headshot chains
counts rise from 1 through 200
the same ten-stage structure repeats across locations
reviews.reason: This duplicates precision-kill progression already represented by Admiral's frozen precision domain and does so through repetitive location templates.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: No per-map headshot ladder, no 1-to-200 escalation and no duplication of frozen Precision Arsenal; only a materially different authored precision operation may be reconsidered.

evidence: legacy README defines per-location Scav headshot chains
counts rise from 1 through 500
round structure is repeated across maps
reviews.reason: This is a high-volume precision farming template with weak distinct product identity and direct overlap with general combat progression.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: Do not port or emulate the map-by-map headshot ladder; reconsider only if a future authored operation has a different tactical purpose.

reviews.sourceBundle: Deep Pockets Legend / Iron Head Legend / Juggernaut Legend / Ultrasound Legend
evidence: legacy README defines hundreds of Legend quests tied to specific gear
each chain repeats eliminations while wearing prescribed equipment
Ultrasound Legend alone contains 72 headset-gated kill quests
reviews.reason: The Legend families multiply storefront unlock content into another gear-restricted kill grid. This is useful only as evidence that equipment constraints exist, not as authored campaign content.
reviews.requiredRewriteBoundary: No gear-by-gear kill matrix and no Legend-scale expansion. A future gear constraint may appear only inside a small operation where the equipment requirement serves the scenario.
